note: Twenty-five pages, seventeen measured regions on fourteen of them, and no deficit: the twelve printed figures and three printed tables each own a region, so the arithmetic closes. Everything quantitative in the paper is a raster screenshot of a plotting tool - twelve of twelve figures, and the pages carry no other image - while all three tables are live text. Two exceptions are declared rather than repaired: Figure 12's caption cannot be read out of the text layer and is typed from the crop, and the newspaper page's photograph is content by the #306 rule.
rules: Seventeen measured regions on fourteen of twenty-five pages resolve into twelve figure rows, three table rows, one uncaptioned photograph and one refusal, and every one of the fifteen printed exhibit numbers owns a region - the census is exact and the deficit is zero. [caption.numbering] is "Figure N:" on all twelve figure rows and "Table N:" on all three table rows, and no caption head prints without its colon.

Caption side is class-fixed with no exception: twelve of twelve figure captions print BELOW the art, 10.9 to 27.8 pt under the region's bottom edge, and three of three table captions print ABOVE the grid, 15.1 to 28.0 pt over the region's top edge - the gap was measured from the caption's own text line to the region edge, and it splits cleanly at the figure/table line. [caption.position] records that split and no row departs from it.

The paper prints fifteen exhibit numbers and no others: Figures 1 to 12 and Tables 1 to 3, with no duplicate number, no number cited but never printed, and no printed number left without a caption. The one uncaptioned object that is content - the photograph on the newspaper page - is recorded with [caption.verbatim] empty, the only row in the record whose caption string is empty.

All twelve figures are embedded rasters rather than drawings: every one of the twelve measured figure regions contains exactly one image and the pages carry no other image anywhere, so nothing in this paper is plotted by the PDF itself. [geometry.family] splits the results accordingly - line 6, other 2, photo-or-raster-image 2, map-or-plan-view 1, flowchart-or-schematic 1, composite-panel 1 - and no figure row takes the value table-grid.

The three tables are live text and their dressing is one recipe: three horizontal rules, no vertical rule, no fill, no merged cell, no zebra row, on all three. Two of the three set their header rule NARROWER than the body rules - Table 2 by 70.8 pt (274.9 against 345.7) and Table 3 by 120.4 pt (293.4 against 413.8) - so the header rule stops inside the table's own width, and only Table 1 runs all three rules to the same width. [table.rule_style] is booktabs on all three rows.

Units never ride in a header: the notation table spells them inside the meaning prose, Table 2 puts the percent sign in each cell and the year unit inside the stub label, and Table 3 puts its units in parentheses inside the stub cells. [table.units_in_header] is false on all three rows and the numbers stand unitless in their columns.

Row counts are the printed counts, read off the text layer rather than off the rules: Table 1 prints one header and sixteen symbol rows whose meanings wrap onto a second line for nine of them, Table 2 one header and two data rows, Table 3 one header and four coordinate rows. [table.rows] carries 17, 3 and 5 and [table.header_rows] is 1 on each.

Three rows sit in a section whose prose is not theirs, and the printed heading order wins over the argument: Table 2 prints on p9 above the 3.3 heading so it belongs to 3.2, while Table 3 and Figure 4 print on p10 below the 3.4 heading that opens that page so they belong to 3.4 even though the paragraph introducing them continues 3.3, and Figure 5 prints at the top of p14 ABOVE the 4.5 heading printed at the foot of that page, so it is filed under 4.4, whose heading is on p13. [place.section_path] follows the heading and every row names the section it prints after - the same field fails in both directions.

Four captions end on a citation marker rather than on their object - Figure 1 on [4], Figures 6 and 7 on [15], Figure 8 on [17] - and one caption carries no object at all: "Figure 5: AHP results" is a method name and nothing else. [caption.verbatim] keeps every marker as printed; [caption.words] runs from 4 (Figure 5) to 14 (Figure 1) across the fifteen captions. By eye every one of them is a single sentence; the one row recorded with [caption.sentences] 2 is Figure 7, where the abbreviation w.r.t. ends in a full stop and the counter splits there - a declared artefact, not a second sentence.

Five of the fifteen numbered exhibits are never named by number in the prose - Figures 3, 8 and 11 and Tables 1 and 3 - and two are named only after they print: Figure 1 prints on p3 and is first cited on p12, nine pages later, the largest negative lead the lane has recorded, and Figure 5 prints on p14 and is first cited on p18. [mention.count] is zero on those five and [mention.lead_pages] is negative on the two late citations.

Figure 12's caption is typed from the crop: the text layer prints the phrase with a space inside T(y) and with the ff ligature replaced by a return-arrow glyph, so no text-layer search matches the printed sentence. [caption.verbatim] carries the printed reading and [caption_source] says typed-from-crop; the other fourteen captions match their line in the text layer exactly.

The last page is the required newspaper article, and its census is one photograph plus one refusal: the aerial sawmill photograph is content and is recorded as an item with an empty caption, while the boxed MCM/ICM nameplate is filed background. The page's own title prints at 20.7 pt and no figure or table number appears anywhere on it, so [caption.numbering] plays no part in either row on p25.
